what: Arthur J. Gallagher is an insurance broker. It arranges property and casualty cover and employee benefits for companies, brokers reinsurance for insurers, and administers claims for self-insured employers.
customers: Small and mid-sized companies above all, plus public bodies and insurers needing reinsurance.
money: commissions and fees for placing insurance and reinsurance
third-party claims administration for self-insured clients
moat: A relationship business where mid-sized clients renew every year, and a long record of acquiring small local brokers and keeping their customers.
risks: Commission income falls when insurance prices soften
It has taken on about $13 billion of debt for acquisitions
Return on invested capital is low because of the price paid for those acquisitions
Integrating dozens of small brokers every year carries execution risk
opportunities: Revenue grew about 21% in the last financial year, mostly through acquisition
Thousands of small brokers remain available to buy in a fragmented market
Brokerage takes no underwriting risk, so earnings are steadier than an insurer's
watch: Organic revenue growth separate from acquisitions, and the pace of deals.
